elements.label: Figure 7.6
elements.description: Combined bar and dot chart with two y-axes. Left axis: 'Cost-effectiveness Index' (0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15). Right axis: 'Size relative to GDP' (0%, 1%, 2%, 3%, 4%, 5%, 6%, 7%, 8%). Legend: 'Effectiveness' (teal bar, left axis) and '% GDP' (orange dot, right axis). Categories, left to right: PIT, Other direct taxes, Social insurance, Cash transfer, Electricity subsidies, Education, Health. No values are printed on the chart; approximate readings are: Effectiveness (bars): PIT ~12.1; Other direct taxes ~6.4; Social insurance ~4.1; Cash transfer ~12.0; Electricity subsidies ~4.9; Education ~8.6; Health ~3.4. % GDP (dots): PIT ~0.9%; Other direct taxes ~0.7%; Social insurance ~7.2%; Cash transfer ~0.8%; Electricity subsidies ~0.6%; Education ~3.8%; Health ~2.7%. Note: Cost-effectiveness index is the marginal contribution to inequality reduction (points of Gini changed) divided by total spending. Source: 2018 VHLSS and World Bank calculations. The pattern: cash transfers and PIT have the highest cost-effectiveness; social insurance has the largest share of GDP but a moderate effectiveness; health has the lowest effectiveness.
